notes.title: Geography — Mount Teskarran
notes.text: Mount Teskarran is the highest peak in the Oruvel Range and stands 5,312 m tall. Its summit is dark basalt shaped like a broken tooth, so locals just call it the Tooth. It was first climbed in 1927 by a surveyor and two shepherds, and 14 glaciers flow down its sides.

notes.title: History — The Treaty of Calvenmoor
notes.text: The Treaty of Calvenmoor was signed in 1687 in a small riverside chapel between the duchies of Aldric and Venmoor. It ended the Salt War, which had dragged on for 11 years over the brine wells along the border. The treaty had 34 articles, most of them about salt taxes and river tolls.

notes.title: Lab Log — Dravenol
notes.text: Dravenol is a clear solvent with a faint green tint that we made by distilling resin from Kestle pine bark, and it smells strongly of pine. In today's lab it boiled at 142 °C and froze solid at -27 °C. Its density came out to 0.91 g/mL, so it floats on water.

notes.title: Astronomy — Comet Vossbrink
notes.text: Comet Vossbrink has a long blue-green tail and was discovered in 1871 by a lighthouse keeper named Ada Vossbrink. It goes around the Sun once every 54 years. It last passed closest to the Sun in 1991.

notes.title: Music — The Kesswynd Lute
notes.text: The Kesswynd lute is a long-necked lute from the fishing villages of the Kesswynd coast, carved from walnut and played with a bone pick. It has 11 strings, and the lowest ones are left open as a drone. The first one was built in 1742 by a ferry captain, and a full-size one weighs about 2.3 kg.

notes.title: Sport — Tarrowball
notes.text: Tarrowball started in the mining towns of the north and is played with a leather ball wrapped in red cord. Each team has 8 players on a hexagonal field that is 72 m across. Each period of play lasts 25 minutes.

notes.title: Economics — The Fennish Crown
notes.text: The Fennish crown became the currency of the island of Fenn in 1874, replacing the old silver skilling at a rate of 36 skillings to one crown. Crown coins are hexagonal and made of brass. They are issued by the Bank of Ostmere, which was founded in 1821.

notes.title: Networking — The Corvel Mesh Protocol
notes.text: The Corvel Mesh Protocol was written by a university radio club to link rooftop antennas into one mesh network. It listens on port 7714 by default and every packet starts with a 24-byte header. A message can be passed along at most 9 hops before it is dropped.

notes.title: Art — The Weeping Orchard
notes.text: The Weeping Orchard is an oil painting by Ilse Varnholt that shows apple trees in heavy rain, painted mostly in ochre and violet. She finished it in 1858 after working on it for 6 years. It is 214 cm wide and hangs in the city museum of Dorrisgate.

notes.title: Language — The Tervish Script
notes.text: The Tervish script was used on the Isle of Terve and is mostly found carved on standing stones. It has 31 letters, all made from small triangular notches, and is read from bottom to top. The oldest known inscription dates to 412 AD, and about 2,600 inscriptions survive.

notes.title: Field Guide — The Ondrel Squid
notes.text: The Ondrel squid lives off the Marrish coast at about 900 m deep and glows pale blue in the dark. It has 12 arms and 2 hearts. Fishermen sometimes find its glassy beak tangled in their nets.

notes.title: Geography — Lake Ombrenne
notes.text: Lake Ombrenne is a cold, very clear lake high in the Sallow Hills, and its water looks almost black from the shore. Its deepest point is 418 m and its surface sits 2,240 m above sea level. It covers 316 km² and only one river, the Ombre, drains it.

notes.title: History — The Battle of Harrowmede
notes.text: The Battle of Harrowmede was fought in 1361 beside the frozen Harrow river, in the middle of winter. About 4,200 soldiers took part, and the fighting went on for 11 days before the river ice broke. It ended the rule of the Corwen family over the valley.

notes.title: Astronomy — The Star Ilvaneth
notes.text: Ilvaneth is an orange star in the constellation of the Heron, best seen from the southern hemisphere in winter. It is 61 light-years from Earth and its surface temperature is about 4,100 K. It is about 2.6 times wider than the Sun.

notes.title: Recipe — Pembury Mutton Pie
notes.text: Pembury mutton pie is my gran's recipe from the Pembury market: diced mutton, leeks and pearl barley under a lard crust brushed with egg. Bake it at 205 °C for 48 minutes, and the filling has to reach 82 °C in the middle before it's safe to serve.

notes.title: Engineering — The Quenby Narrows Bridge
notes.text: The Quenby Narrows Bridge is a teal suspension bridge across the Quenby inlet, built by the Harlan shipyards. It opened in 1952 and its main span is 917 m long. Each of its towers is 128 m tall.
